definitions.explanation: In anthropology, the earliest stage of human ancestors, such as the australopithecines, regarded as a link between apes and humans. The oldest of the textbook stages {猿人|えんじん} → {原人|げんじん} → {旧人|きゅうじん} → {新人|しんじん}.

examples.japanese: {猿人|えんじん}の{化石|かせき}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: Fossils of an early hominid were found.

examples.japanese: {猿人|えんじん}は{二足歩行|にそくほこう}をしていたと{考|かんが}えられている。
examples.english: Australopithecines are thought to have walked on two legs.

examples.japanese: {人類|じんるい}の{進化|しんか}は{猿人|えんじん}から{原人|げんじん}へと{段階的|だんかいてき}に{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: Human evolution proceeded in stages from ape-men to early humans.

notes:
A technical term in physical anthropology for the earliest grade of human ancestor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猿人|えんじん}の{化石|かせき}: hominid fossils
- {初期|しょき}の{猿人|えんじん}: early hominids
- {猿人|えんじん}から{進化|しんか}する: to evolve from ape-men

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {原人|げんじん}: Homo erectus stage — the next grade after {猿人|えんじん}
- {類人猿|るいじんえん}: great ape — living apes such as the gorilla and chimpanzee, not human ancestors
